newsitem.title: EGYPT: $100 mln loan for CIB to be at LIBOR+40 basis pts.
newsitem.headline: $100 mln loan for CIB to be at LIBOR+40 basis pts.

text.p: A $100 million three-year syndicated loan for Commercial International Bank (CIB) of Egypt will be at LIBOR plus 40 basis points, CIB managing director Adel El-Labban said on Thursday.
The transaction costs for the loan will amount to a little over 50 basis points, less than it would cost to raise the money through a floating rate note, he told Reuters.

Labban said on Wednesday CIB had mandated Chase Investment Bank Ltd and Union Bank of Switzerland SBGZ.Z to arrange the syndicated loan, the first by an Egyptian borrower for 15 years. ING Barings and Commerzbank are joint lead arrangers and invitations are going out to form the co-arrangers group.

Labban said on Thursday it opted for the loan both because of the relatively low costing and because it would be quicker than issuing floating rate notes, which would require CIB to go through a rating process.
CIB, Egypt's largest private-sector bank and the only one with shares traded internationally, is also planning to issue a domestic Egyptian pound floating rate note.
"Opportunities to issue Eurodebt securities in the second half of the year are also under consideration subject to favourable market conditions," it added on Wednesday.
